title: Brauer splitting theorem over a field containing exponent roots of unity
statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $N\geq1$, and suppose $K$ contains an element $\zeta$ with $\zeta^N=1$ and $\zeta^j\neq1$ for every integer $0<j<N$. Let $G$ be a finite group such that $g^N=1$ for all $g\in G$. Define $K[G]$ as the $K$-vector space with basis $[g]$ for $g\in G$ and bilinear multiplication $[g][h]=[gh]$. There are integers $r\geq1$, $d_1,\ldots,d_r\geq1$ and a $K$-algebra isomorphism $K[G]\cong\prod_{i=1}^r M_{d_i}(K)$ [def-weil-matrix].

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, representation-theoretic input cited to Serre 1978, 12 section 2.3 and 13 section 14.4. The auxiliary characteristic-zero splitting-field input is Brauer’s theorem (a field containing the exponent roots of unity is a splitting field); Serre is WANTED and this theorem is left statement-only.

proof.text: Put $A=K[G]$. Its displayed basis is finite and contains the nonzero vector $[1]$. Since $K$ has characteristic zero and $|G|\ge1$, $|G|\cdot1_K\ne0$. By [lem-per-maschke-finite-group-algebra], $A$ is semisimple. Apply [lem-per-semisimple-algebra-matrix-division] to obtain $A\cong\prod_{i=1}^r M_{d_i}(D_i)$ with $d_i>0$ and finite-dimensional division $K$-algebras $D_i$. Necessarily $r\ge1$, since the empty product is the zero ring whereas $[1]\ne0$. Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $K$ by [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique].

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, field-splitting input for representation lifting before equation (5); agent-written argument, semisimple decomposition and choice of coefficient extension

proof.text: Regard $K$ as a subfield of $\Omega$ using its injective structural map. The $N$ elements $1,\zeta,\ldots,\zeta^{N-1}$ are distinct: equality of the $a$th and $b$th powers for $0\le a<b<N$ would give $\zeta^{b-a}=1$. They are roots of $X^N-1$, and therefore exhaust its roots in $\Omega$; successively factoring out these $N$ linear factors leaves the monic constant polynomial $1$. Thus every $N$th root of unity in $\Omega$ belongs to $K$.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, field-splitting input for representation lifting before equation (5); agent-written argument, roots of unity

proof.text: Use [lem-per-brauer-monomial-induction] over $\Omega$. For each subgroup $H$ and each linear character $\lambda:H\to\Omega^\times$ occurring there, $\lambda(h)^N=\lambda(h^N)=1$. Step 2 shows that $\lambda$ has values in $K^\times$. Its induced representation has a $K$-model: choose representatives $t$ of $G/H$, take the $K$-basis $e_t$, and, when $a t=t\prime h$, set $a e_t=\lambda(h)e_{t\prime}$. Uniqueness of $t\prime,h$ and $\lambda(hh\prime)=\lambda(h)\lambda(h\prime)$ verify the group action. The quotient in the cited node has this same basis, by $e_{th}=\lambda(h)e_t$. On extending to $\Omega$ the action matrices are identical. Hence every monomial class, and consequently every class in $R_\Omega(G)$, is an integer combination of scalar extensions of $K$-representations.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, field-splitting input for representation lifting before equation (5); agent-written argument, Brauer induction and explicit coset models

proof.text: For clarity, the groups $R$ here are generated by isomorphism classes modulo direct-sum relations, as in [lem-per-semisimple-scalar-extension-kzero-criterion]. A $K[G]$-module is exactly a $K$-linear $G$-representation: restrict the action to $[g]$, and conversely extend it linearly. These operations are inverse and preserve sums and isomorphisms. The map $\Omega\otimes_K A\to\Omega[G]$, $x\otimes\sum_g a_g[g]\mapsto\sum_g(xa_g)[g]$, is an algebra isomorphism with inverse $\sum_g b_g[g]\mapsto\sum_g b_g\otimes[g]$, by the bilinear relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Under these identifications Step 3 proves precisely the surjectivity of $s:R(A)\to R(A_\Omega)$.

source.place: Expose X Proposition 1.2, printed p.138, field-splitting input for representation lifting before equation (5); agent-written argument, identify scalar-extension classes

proof.text: Characteristic zero persists in $\Omega$, so [lem-per-maschke-finite-group-algebra] makes $A_\Omega\cong\Omega[G]$ semisimple. All hypotheses of [lem-per-semisimple-scalar-extension-kzero-criterion] now hold for the decomposition in Step 1. It gives bijective structural maps $K\to D_i$. Their inverses are $K$-algebra isomorphisms $D_i\to K$. Apply these inverses entry by entry to each matrix factor and compose with the isomorphism of Step 1. This yields the required $K[G]\cong\prod_{i=1}^r M_{d_i}(K)$, with $r,d_i\ge1$.
